newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi confirms Stet privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi confirms Stet privatisation.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi confirmed on Friday that privatisations of telecoms giant Stet motorway manager Autostrade and telephone directory publisher Seat would go ahead.
Prodi told a news conference the government had no immediate plans to privatise electricity utility Enel but said its privatisation certainly was not ruled out.
"(Enel's sale) is not programmed but it is not excluded. It's in the pipeline," Prodi told the news conference.
Prodi also confirmed the sale of the third tranche of energy giant Eni would go ahead. The Italian Treasury has said it intends to offer the third tranche of Eni on June 23-27.
Telecommunications holding Stet is expected to be privatised in the second half of this year after its merger with telephone service operator Telecom Italia is complete.
The Treasury said earlier this month final offers from three consortiums bidding for Seat must be in by the end of June.
Italian state industrial holding Iri is currently studying what timetable to set for the sale of motorway company Autostrade, whose sale had been due for launch by the end of June.
A company source said this week no decision had yet been taken on whether to delay the sale possibly until September.
